hook.text: Download a file. The website shows a checksum. Compute yours. If they match, the file is intact. If not, re-download.

buildup.text: A checksum is a short digest computed from the data. It catches more error patterns than a single parity bit.

discovery.text: Internet checksums add 16-bit words and take the complement. It's fast, simple, and catches most random errors.

twist.text: Checksums can miss systematic errors. Reordering data blocks may produce the same sum. They're not foolproof.

climax.text: TCP, UDP, and IP all use checksums. Every internet packet is checked before delivery.

punchline.text: A short summary that catches corruption. Quick and cheap.

quiz.question: Why are checksums not foolproof?
options: Some error patterns produce the same checksum
They only work on small files
